content:
Ben Carter: landing page copy review thread — pls paste last-minute edits here so we don’t lose track in comments. Need to lock headline + CTA today for tomorrow’s build.

Ben Carter: Current draft in Drive (comment-only for now): https://drive.google.com/.../landing-page-copy-draft-regulated

Ben Carter: Key open question: primary CTA = “Request security review” vs “Download benchmark”? We can keep the other as secondary.

Soojin Lee: Dropping proposed headline + subhead. Trying to keep it compliance-safe + not overpromise.

Soojin Lee: Headline option A:
“Run LLM inference for regulated workloads — without sacrificing latency or control.”
Subhead:
“Deploy in hosted, dedicated, or private environments with auditability, access controls, and predictable performance.”

Soojin Lee: Headline option B:
“Private & dedicated LLM inference for security- and compliance-driven teams.”
Subhead:
“VPC/on‑prem options, audit logs, and operational tooling to keep production stable under real load.”

Ethan Wallace: +1 on B. A reads a little generic / could be any vendor.

Ethan Wallace: Quick nit: “regulated workloads” should be defined somewhere. Maybe a small callout: “Examples: financial services, healthcare (PHI-adjacent), insurance, public sector.”

Naomi Feldman: Agree w/ definition callout. Also please avoid “HIPAA-ready” / “HIPAA compliant” anywhere on page. We can say “supports HIPAA-aligned deployments” ONLY if we pair it with “implementation depends on customer configuration + scope.”

Dr. Aisha Rahman: +1. Also avoid implying certifications we don’t have. If we mention SOC 2 / ISO, it needs to match the Security FAQ language.

Elliot Price: Linking the approved phrasing from the Security FAQ / evidence pack index. If we copy/paste lines, they should be identical.
- Security FAQ: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/.../regulated-workloads-security-faq
- Evidence pack index: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/.../abm-pilot-security-evidence-pack-index

Elliot Price: Also FYI docs PR is staging the page next to the FAQ. If we pick CTA = security review, I can add a cross-link to the FAQ and evidence pack request form.

Ben Carter: noted. For CTA, I’m leaning “Request a security + architecture review” to optimize for meetings, but benchmark download tends to convert on ads.

Tyler Benson: From attribution POV: meeting CTA gives us cleaner tracking + faster qualification. Download is good but we’ll need nurture + score thresholds. If we do download, we should gate with work email + role + “deployment preference” question.

Soojin Lee: What if we do:
Primary CTA: “Request a security review”
Secondary link CTA: “Download the regulated inference benchmark (PDF)”

Soojin Lee: Keeps the page enterprise-forward and still offers self-serve value.

Ethan Wallace: That works. I’d tweak “security review” to feel less scary. Maybe “Security & compliance Q&A” or “Security review call”.

Naomi Feldman: “Security review call” is fine. Just make it clear what they get: “walkthrough of controls + evidence pack request process.” But don’t promise we’ll share everything immediately.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Suggest copy:
“Book a 20‑minute security & architecture review”
Then small text: “We’ll cover deployment options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), audit logging, encryption, and evidence pack access.”

Ben Carter: ok, tentatively locking:
Primary CTA button: “Book a security & architecture review”
Secondary text link: “Download benchmark”

Ben Carter: Can we also tighten the “controls” section? Current bullets:
- SSO/SAML
- Audit logs
- Encryption
- Data retention
- Residency
Feels too list-y.

Soojin Lee: Proposed rewrite for that block:
Section title: “Controls and evidence for regulated environments”
Bullets:
- “Access controls: RBAC plus SSO (SAML) support”
- “Auditability: exportable audit logs for user/admin actions”
- “Encryption: in transit + at rest; customer-managed keys available for Private deployments”
- “Retention & residency: configurable options by deployment mode”

Soojin Lee: Footnote: “Specific controls vary by product and configuration; Redwood will confirm scope during security review.”

Elliot Price: Please change “exportable audit logs” to “audit logs with export options” (less absolute). Also “user/admin actions” is good — avoids implying full app-layer logging.

Naomi Feldman: +1. Also on “retention & residency”: don’t say “configurable” without qualification. Better:
“Retention & residency: options available depending on region and deployment.”

Ethan Wallace: On proof points section, we have line: “No data is used for training.” Are we keeping?

Naomi Feldman: That’s risky as a blanket statement. We should align with standard language (varies by product, contract, and settings). Use the FAQ snippet instead.

Elliot Price: Correct, use approved line:
“Customer data is handled according to the selected product, configuration, and contractual terms. Details available under NDA during security review.”

Ben Carter: Got it. Removing the absolute “no training” sentence from LP.

Ben Carter: Another copy tweak request from Sales: include Dedicated vs Private guidance, but keep it short.

Soojin Lee: Suggested 2-up card copy:
Card 1: “Dedicated”
“Reserved GPU capacity with data isolation and predictable throughput. Ideal when you need stronger guarantees without full private networking.”
Card 2: “Private (VPC / on‑prem)”
“Customer-managed networking and security boundaries for regulated deployments. Ideal for strict residency, integration, and audit requirements.”

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Looks good. Avoid “guarantees” though. Maybe “predictable performance targets” / “SLA options”.

Soojin Lee: Updated:
Dedicated: “Reserved GPU capacity with isolation and predictable performance targets. SLA options available.”

Tyler Benson: CTA wording in forms: if button says “Book a security & architecture review”, the form headline should match exactly for conversion.

Ben Carter: +1. Ethan can you update the form copy to match?

Ethan Wallace: yep. Form headline: “Book a security & architecture review”
Form fields: Work email, Company, Role (dropdown), Deployment interest (Hosted/Dedicated/Private/Not sure), Timeline.

Ben Carter: Perfect.

Elliot Price: One more: if we’re linking the “Download benchmark” from the LP, we should add a small disclaimer under the link: “Benchmark methodology and results in PDF” so it doesn’t read like a vague asset.

Ben Carter: Done. Locking decisions:
- Headline: Option B (“Private & dedicated LLM inference…”)
- Primary CTA: “Book a security & architecture review”
- Secondary CTA: “Download the regulated inference benchmark”

Ben Carter: Please add any final redlines in next ~2 hrs. I’m pushing changes into the docs PR after.

Naomi Feldman: No further redlines from Security if the “HIPAA” term is removed and the footnote about scope stays in.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Same. If anyone wants to add a compliance badge row, run it by Security first — don’t want a last-minute “SOC2/ISO” mismatch.

Ben Carter: :thumbsup: thanks all. Moving to PR review once I paste final copy.
